sentences.en: Good morning, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家早上好。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: Now, at the university, you, as students, are often called on to perform many types of listening tasks: listening in a group discussion, listening to a teacher on a one-to-one basis, and listening to academic lectures.
sentences.zh: 在大学里，作为学生，你们经常需要完成各种听力任务：听小组讨论、与老师一对一交谈，以及听学术讲座。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: So what I’m going to talk about today is what a listener needs to be able to do in order to comprehend an academic lecture efficiently.
sentences.zh: 因此，今天我要讲的是，听众要具备哪些能力，才能高效地理解一场学术讲座。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: OK.
sentences.zh: 好。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: What do you need to do in order to understand the lecture?
sentences.zh: 要听懂讲座，你需要做些什么呢？
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: Now there are four things that I’m going to talk about.
sentences.zh: 接下来，我要谈四个方面。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: The first thing is that you need to be aware of all of the parts of the language that carry meaning.
sentences.zh: 首先，你需要意识到，语言中所有能够传达意义的组成部分都值得注意。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: You all know that words carry meaning.
sentences.zh: 你们都知道，词语能够传达意义。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: So you've got to be aware of the vocabulary of the language, but there are some other features.
sentences.zh: 所以，你必须了解这门语言的词汇，但除此之外，还有其他特征。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: For one thing, you need to be aware of stress.
sentences.zh: 例如，你需要注意重音。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: Let me give you an example.
sentences.zh: 我来举个例子。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: “I went to the bar.” “I went to the bar.” It makes a difference.
sentences.zh: “我去了酒吧。”“是我去了酒吧。”这样读，意思就有所不同。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: In the second example, I’m stressing the fact that it was me and not someone else so that this means stress has some meaning.
sentences.zh: 在第二个例子里，我强调的是去酒吧的人是我，而不是别人；这就说明，重音本身也传递意义。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: Now the next thing you might want to listen for is intonation.
sentences.zh: 接下来，你可能需要留意的是语调。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: For example, if I say “He came.” “He came?” There are two different meanings.
sentences.zh: 比如，我说“他来了。”“他来了？”这两句话表达的是不同的意思。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: One is a statement, the other one is a question.
sentences.zh: 一个是陈述，另一个是提问。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: And another thing you need to listen for is rhythm.
sentences.zh: 你还需要留意节奏。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: For instance, “Can you see, Mary?” versus “Can you see Mary?” da da DA da... da da da DA da.
sentences.zh: 比如，“玛丽，你看得见吗？”与“你看得见玛丽吗？”——哒哒哒哒……哒哒哒哒。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: Those two mean something different.
sentences.zh: 这两种说法表达的意思不同。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: In the first one, they are talking directly to Mary, while the second one means “Can you see Mary... over there?”
sentences.zh: 第一种说法是直接对玛丽说话，而第二种则是问：“你看得见那边的玛丽吗？”
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: Now the next thing you must do when you listen is that you need to add information that the lecturer expects you to add.
sentences.zh: 接下来，听的时候你还必须补充一些信息，而讲课人会预期你能够自行补上这些信息。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: All lecturers assume that they share some information with their audience and that their audience does not need them to explain every word.
sentences.zh: 所有讲课人都会假定，自己与听众掌握着某些共同信息，因此不必逐字解释每个词。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: And listeners have an ability to add this information due to two sources of information.
sentences.zh: 听众能够补充这些信息，是因为他们有两种信息来源。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: That is, one, their knowledge of a particular subject; and, two, their knowledge or experience of the world.
sentences.zh: 第一，是对某个特定学科的了解；第二，是对世界的知识或生活经验。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: So remember: listening is not a matter of just absorbing the speaker’s words; the listener has to do more than that.
sentences.zh: 所以，请记住：听讲并不是仅仅接收说话人的话语，听众还需要做得更多。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: The listener is not a tape recorder, absorbing the speaker’s words and putting them into his or her brain.
sentences.zh: 听众不是录音机，不会只是接收说话人的话，再把这些话存进脑海。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: Rather, listening involves hearing the speaker's words and reinterpreting them, adding information if necessary.
sentences.zh: 相反，听的过程包括听见说话人的话、重新理解这些话，并在必要时补充信息。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: So the meaning is not in the word alone, rather it is in the person who uses it or responds to it so that the second thing that a listener must do— add information that the lecturer assumes that they share.
sentences.zh: 因此，意义并不只存在于词语本身，也存在于使用这些词语、或对其作出回应的人身上。所以，听众要做的第二件事，就是补充讲课人假定双方都知道的信息。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: OK.
sentences.zh: 好。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: The third thing that a listener needs to do, and this is to me the most important thing of all, and that’s to predict as you listen.
sentences.zh: 听众需要做的第三件事——在我看来也是最重要的一件事——就是边听边预测。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: Now let me give you two reasons why you have to predict.
sentences.zh: 现在，我来解释为什么要预测，原因有两个。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: For one thing, if you predict it helps you overcome noise.
sentences.zh: 首先，预测有助于你克服噪声的干扰。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: What do I mean by noise?
sentences.zh: 这里所说的“噪声”是什么意思呢？
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: Maybe there’s noise outside and you can’t hear me.
sentences.zh: 也许外面很吵，以至于你听不见我说话。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: Maybe you're in the back of the room and you can’t hear all that well.
sentences.zh: 也许你坐在教室后面，听得不太清楚。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: Maybe the microphone doesn’t work.
sentences.zh: 也许麦克风出了故障。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: Maybe there’s noise inside your head.
sentences.zh: 也许噪声来自你的脑海。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: By that I mean maybe you're thinking of something else.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你可能正在想着其他事情。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: And then all of a sudden, you'll remember “Oh, I’ve got to listen.” By being able to predict during the lecture, you can just keep listening to the lecture and not lose the idea of what’s going on.
sentences.zh: 随后，你会突然想起来：“哦，我得认真听。”如果你能在听讲时进行预测，就能继续跟上讲座，而不会失去对当前内容的理解。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: So predicting is important to help you overcome outside noise and inside noise.
sentences.zh: 所以，预测对于克服外部噪声和内心干扰都很重要。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: And another reason that predicting is important is because it saves you time.
sentences.zh: 预测之所以重要，还有一个原因，那就是它能节省时间。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: Now when you listen you need time to think about the information, relate it to old ideas, take notes, and if you’re only keeping up with what I’m saying or what the lecturer’s saying, you have no time to do that.
sentences.zh: 听讲时，你需要时间来思考信息、把它与已有的想法联系起来，以及记笔记；如果你只是勉强跟上我或讲课人的讲话，就没有时间做这些事了。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: And I’ll bet a lot of you are having that problem right now because it’s so hard just to follow everything I’m saying, that you don’t have time to note down ideas.
sentences.zh: 我敢说，你们中很多人现在就有这个问题：光是跟上我说的全部内容，就已经很费力了，因而没有时间记下要点。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: So predicting saves you time.
sentences.zh: 因此，预测可以节省时间。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: If you can guess what I’m going to say, you're able to take notes, you’re able to think, you have more time.
sentences.zh: 如果你能猜到我接下来会说什么，就能记笔记，也能进行思考，你就拥有更多时间。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: OK?
sentences.zh: 明白吗？
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: And there are two types of predictions that you can make: predictions of content and predictions of organization.
sentences.zh: 你可以作出两类预测：对内容的预测，以及对组织结构的预测。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: Let me give you an example in terms of content.
sentences.zh: 我先举一个预测内容的例子。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: If you hear the words “Because he loved to cook, his favorite room was...” what would you expect?
sentences.zh: 如果你听到“因为他喜欢做饭，他最喜欢的房间是……”这些话，你会预期接下来出现什么词？
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: Kitchen.
sentences.zh: 厨房。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: You can guess this because you know people cook in the kitchen.
sentences.zh: 你能猜到这一点，是因为你知道人们通常在厨房里做饭。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: OK?
sentences.zh: 明白吗？
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: And you can also predict organization.
sentences.zh: 你也可以预测讲话的组织结构。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: So if I was going to tell you a story, you'd expect me to tell you why the story is important, give you a setting for the story.
sentences.zh: 比如，如果我要给你讲一个故事，你就会期待我先说明这个故事为什么重要，并交代故事发生的背景。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: So you have expectations of what the speaker is going to talk about and how the speaker will organize his or her words.
sentences.zh: 因此，对于说话人接下来要谈什么，以及他或她会如何组织语言，你都会有所预期。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: Now let’s come to the last thing a listener must do: the listener must evaluate, as he or she is listening, decide what’s important, what’s not, decide how something relates to something else.
sentences.zh: 现在来看听众必须做的最后一件事：边听边评价，判断什么重要、什么不重要，以及某件事与另一件事之间有什么联系。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: OK?
sentences.zh: 明白吗？
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: There are again two reasons for this.
sentences.zh: 这样做同样有两个原因。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: The first one is evaluating helps you to decide what to take notes about: what's important to write down? what’s not important to write down?
sentences.zh: 第一个原因是，评价能够帮助你决定哪些内容值得记笔记：什么值得写下来？什么不值得写下来？
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: And the second reason is that evaluating helps you to keep information.
sentences.zh: 第二个原因是，评价有助于你记住信息。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: Studies have shown that we retain more information if ideas are connected to one another rather than just individually remembered.
sentences.zh: 研究表明，如果各种想法彼此关联，而不是各自孤立地记忆，我们就能记住更多信息。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: So for example, if I give you five ideas that are not related to one another, that’s much more difficult to remember than five ideas that are related.
sentences.zh: 比如，我给你五个彼此不相关的想法，它们会比五个相互关联的想法难记得多。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: So you can see evaluating helps you to remember information better because it connects ideas to one another.
sentences.zh: 所以，你可以看到，评价把各种想法联系在一起，因此能帮助你更好地记住信息。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: OK.
sentences.zh: 好。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: From what I’ve said so far, you can see there’s a lot involved in listening to lectures: language awareness, adding information, making predictions and evaluations.
sentences.zh: 从刚才的内容可以看出，听讲座涉及很多事情：语言意识、补充信息、进行预测和作出评价。
sentences.speaker: lecturer

sentences.en: I hope these will be useful to you in lecture comprehension.
sentences.zh: 我希望这些方法能有助于你们理解讲座。
sentences.speaker: lecturer
